title: Console final polish — warm the off-bridge Qwen renderer at webapp startup + default to cupy when a GPU is present

context.prior: CYCLE 521 (AUTONOMOUS_STATE.md) + research/findings/raw/_console_live_debug_fixes.json: the SK brain-load was fixed (~9.8min -> 0.7s). The remaining ~58s FIRST-turn cost is the off-bridge Qwen-0.5B renderer MODEL load (transformers from_pretrained -> GPU + spiking-op calibration), one-time per webapp session; warm turns are ~1.7s.
context.goal: Pay the ~58s Qwen model load at webapp STARTUP (background, non-blocking) so the FIRST chat turn is fast; and make a bare `uvicorn webapp.server:app` use the cupy (GPU) backend when a CUDA GPU is present instead of the ~20x-slower numpy-CPU backend.

changes.what: Added a third `@app.on_event('startup')` hook `_warm_chat_brain` that pre-builds the off-bridge Qwen renderer (and the DEFAULT ChatBrain) ONCE in a background daemon thread, so uvicorn reports startup-complete promptly while the model loads.

lines.build_chat_brain_reuse: ~2956-2964 (`_build_chat_brain` now uses `_get_warm_qwen_renderer()` for the qwen renderer instead of constructing a fresh `QwenRenderer(seed=42)`)
lines.import_trim: QwenRenderer dropped from the `_build_chat_brain` import block; now imported locally inside `_get_warm_qwen_renderer` (its only use site)

changes.mechanism: The QwenRenderer (which constructs SpikingQwenFaculty -> from_pretrained model load + calibration, the ~58s cost) is now a PROCESS-WIDE shared singleton built once under a double-checked lock. The startup hook builds the DEFAULT ChatBrain (brain='tiny-demo' + the resolved renderer), which (a) pays the model load once and (b) caches the default ChatBrain under the SAME cache key brain_chat() looks up for a default first turn: ('default','tiny-demo',<renderer>). So a default first turn hits the warm cache outright; and because the qwen renderer is the shared singleton, even a first turn that picks a DIFFERENT brain reuses the already-loaded model (only its small brain build remains).
guards: only warms the qwen MODEL when `_default_brain_renderer()` actually resolves to 'qwen' (a GPU host on the cupy backend); on a GPU-less / stub-renderer host the hook logs + returns (no model download, the stub builds instantly on first turn)
the warm runs in a daemon thread (never blocks boot, never blocks process exit)
any failure (no GPU, qwen/torch unavailable, model not downloaded) is swallowed -> the chat endpoint builds on the first turn / falls back to the stub renderer exactly as before
_get_warm_qwen_renderer uses double-checked locking so a concurrent startup-warm + first-turn build the model only ONCE

changes.what: Added a module-load-time block (right after the path constants, BEFORE any FastAPI/sim/cupy use) that `os.environ.setdefault('SIM_BACKEND','cupy')` ONLY IF a CUDA GPU is detected.
changes.lines: ~44-80 (new `def _cuda_gpu_present()` + the `if 'SIM_BACKEND' not in os.environ and _cuda_gpu_present(): os.environ.setdefault('SIM_BACKEND','cupy')` block)
changes.mechanism: All sim/cupy imports in server.py are lazy (inside endpoint handlers + _build_chat_brain), so a module-load-time SIM_BACKEND set wins the FIRST `get_backend()` resolution. `_cuda_gpu_present()` tries cupy's runtime getDeviceCount first (matches the production backend), then torch.cuda.is_available() as a fallback; any import/probe error -> False (conservative).
guards: `setdefault` never clobbers an explicit SIM_BACKEND -> `SIM_BACKEND=numpy uvicorn ...` stays numpy (CPU-portable path preserved)
the `and` short-circuits: when SIM_BACKEND is ALREADY set (incl. numpy), `_cuda_gpu_present()` is NEVER called -> no cupy/torch import on a deliberately-numpy launch
only sets cupy when a GPU is genuinely found; else the env is left unset so sim.backend auto-detects -> numpy on a GPU-less host

validation_logic_cpu_only.cache_key_match: VERIFIED — brain_chat() builds cache_key=(req.session, req.brain, _default_brain_renderer().lower()); BrainChatRequest defaults session='default', brain='tiny-demo', renderer=None. The warm hook builds ('default','tiny-demo',_default_brain_renderer()). _default_brain_renderer() returns already-lowercase 'qwen'/'stub' so .lower() is a no-op -> keys are IDENTICAL. A default first turn hits the warm cache.
validation_logic_cpu_only.double_checked_locking_unit_test: PASS — 8 concurrent callers (startup-warm racing a fast first turn) -> the mock model build_count == 1 and all callers share the SAME instance; a subsequent call returns the cached instance with no new build.
validation_logic_cpu_only.renderer_default_logic: _default_brain_renderer(): backend='cupy' (now set by change #2 on a GPU host) passes the `backend != 'cupy'` guard, torch.cuda.is_available() -> returns 'qwen'. On a numpy/CPU host SIM_BACKEND is unset -> backend='' -> torch check -> 'stub'. Consistent.
validation_logic_cpu_only.anti_cheat_behavior_unchanged: The ONLY chat-path change is reusing a SHARED QwenRenderer instance (same class, seed=42) instead of constructing a fresh one each build. QwenRenderer.render_svo is stateless across calls (re-prompts per fact), so the surface form + the gate/constrain/VERIFY no-confab moat are byte-identical. brain_chat()'s GATE -> render -> verify flow, the recalled_svo, abstained, verified fields, and the rich path are all untouched. Only the FIRST-turn LATENCY improves.

sim_edit_flag: NONE — git diff --name-only -- sim/ is empty. webapp-only change.
honest_notes: Warming is done in a BACKGROUND DAEMON THREAD (not a blocking startup) so uvicorn boots promptly and the dashboard + all other endpoints are usable immediately; if a first chat turn arrives DURING the warm, the shared-singleton lock serializes it so the model still loads exactly once (the turn waits on the same load it would have triggered itself — no double load, no extra latency vs. cold).
On a GPU-less / stub-renderer host the warm hook is a deliberate no-op (logs that the renderer is GPU-free); the stub ChatBrain is cheap to build on the first turn so there is nothing worth warming.
Controller does the live restart + first-turn timing (this session did NOT restart or curl the running webapp).

The model files must already be downloaded for the warm to be instant-after-startup; if not present, from_pretrained downloads on first warm (one-time), and the guard swallows any failure -> falls back to the stub renderer.

controller_restart_and_time_command.note: Restart the webapp on cupy and time the FIRST chat turn to confirm it is now fast (the renderer is warmed at startup). Wait until the startup log prints '[webapp] startup: Qwen renderer WARM in <N>s' BEFORE sending the first turn, OR send it immediately to confirm the singleton lock makes the cold first turn no slower than the warm load.
controller_restart_and_time_command.powershell_restart: Stop the current :8765 server, then: $env:SIM_BACKEND='cupy'; python -m uvicorn webapp.server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765   # (or `uvicorn webapp.server:app --port 8765` — change #2 now auto-sets cupy when the GPU is present)
controller_restart_and_time_command.time_first_turn_bash: time curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/brain-chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"session":"default","brain":"tiny-demo","message":"what does the dog do?"}'
controller_restart_and_time_command.expected: After the startup log shows 'Qwen renderer WARM', the FIRST POST should return in ~1.7s (the warm-turn latency) instead of ~58s; the answer + abstained/verified fields are unchanged.
